citation: Van Daele, F., Bonte, D. (2024). Living Dunes: a process-based model for developing Digital Twins of coastal dune dynamics. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.14225553

dedupe_keys.name: living dunes process based model for coastal dune digital twins

description: Living Dunes is a spatially explicit, process-based Python model that couples dune vegetation dynamics with aeolian sand transport and key environmental drivers, intended for building digital twins of coastal dune dynamics. In collaboration with the Dunefront and SUSANA projects, which aim to improve coastal protection by optimising nature-based solutions, trait data for dune-building plant species across Europe, covering germination, growth, dispersal and mortality, are being harmonised to parameterise the model, and demographic processes are driven by environmental variables interpolated from cloud APIs. The authors' site offers interactive and advanced simulation modes in the browser for adjusting parameters, running scenarios, viewing dune evolution and exporting results, aimed at coastal managers, engineers and researchers. It is developed by Frederik Van Daele and Dries Bonte at Ghent University; the Zenodo software records from November 2024 (version 0.1, CC BY 4.0) hold metadata only, and the site states that a beta version will be released open source on GitHub. Caveats: code is not yet downloadable, and parameterisation is ongoing. It supports climate adaptation and resilience planning for dune-based coastal protection and digital twin development; a related record is the Coastal Hazard Wheel.
